items.title: El Niño to bring milder temperatures, and more potholes, to Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga officials say a potentially historic El Niño that’s expected to bring milder temperatures to southern Ontario this fall and winter will also impact the city in other ways. Coupled with climate change, “which is warming ocean waters,” the El Niño effect could be even stronger, the City of Mississauga said this week. “In Mississauga, that could mean a slower start to winter and more days when temperatures rise above and fall below freezing,” city officials said Thursday, adding some city services “may be delayed or look different than usual” as a result. “A strong El Niño could bring a longer, milder fall and a higher chance of extreme weather to Mississauga,” the city continued. Beyond Mississauga and southern Ontario, weather experts have said El Niño, a natural weather pattern caused by warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures that can affect global weather, will also have a strong impact across much of Canada in the coming months. ” Residents should become familiar with the municipality’s online emergency preparedness guide, officials added.

items.title: Coroner’s inquest into death of Jamal Francique postponed by a day
items.summary: Last Updated November 12, 2026 at 10:47 am A coroner’s inquest meant to examine the circumstances surrounding the death of a man who was shot in the head by police west of Toronto nearly seven years ago has been postponed by a day. The inquest into the death of Jamal Francique was scheduled to begin Thursday morning, but a notice on the inquest website says it will now start Friday. The notice says details on the delay will be provided at that time. Francique died in hospital on Jan. 9, 2020, two days after police shot him during a botched arrest in Mississauga, Ont. He was 28. About a year later, Ontario’s police watchdog cleared the Peel regional police officers of wrongdoing, saying the officer who opened fire reported fearing for his life when Francique drove at him. The Special Investigations Unit said there were aspects of the officer’s behaviour that gave rise to questions, however, such as the decision to place himself in the vicinity of a fleeing driver. The SIU said police were investigating Francique for allegedly dealing drugs and possessing a firearm at the time, but couldn’t confirm those allegations so they decided to arrest him for allegedly breaching bail conditions. The agency said plainclothes officers in unmarked cars waited for Francique to get into his car outside his home.

items.title: Mississauga suspect linked to February shooting of 2 men arrested after returning to Canada, say Peel police
items.summary: Two victims — 19 and 21 — were seriously hurt during a shooting at a plaza near Kennedy Road and Eglington Avenue East on Feb. 21, police say. A Mississauga man, 22, has been charged with attempted murder, aggravated assault, discharge firearm with intent and four other gun crimes. A suspect wanted in connection with a Mississauga shooting earlier this year that left two men hurt has been arrested after returning to Canada, say Peel police. Two victims — 19 and 21 — were seriously hurt during a shooting at a plaza near Kennedy Road and Eglinton Avenue East on Feb. 21, police say. Both of the men survived, added the Peel force. The suspect was later identified as a 22-year-old Mississauga man and a Canada-wide warrant for his arrest was issued in May. It was later determined, say police, that the suspect left the country following the shooting. According to police, the suspect returned to Canada on Nov. 9 and turned himself in.

items.title: Canada-Wide Warrant Ends as Mississauga Double-Shooting Suspect Turns Himself In
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a man wanted on a Canada-wide warrant in connection with a double shooting earlier this year in Mississauga has turned himself in to detectives. According to insauga.com, Carlos Rodriguez-Rodriguez, 22, of Mississauga, surrendered to police on Nov. 9 after returning to the country; officers did not say where he had been. The outlet reported Rodriguez-Rodriguez faces multiple charges tied to a Feb. 21 shooting at a plaza near Kennedy Road and Eglinton Avenue East. Detectives from Peel police's 12 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau identified him as a suspect in the months after the shooting, insauga.com said. Police issued the Canada-wide warrant for his arrest in May, after investigators determined he had left the country following the February shooting, according to the report.

items.title: Mon Gat'ô Pâtisserie Trades Port Credit Storefront for Streetsville Space
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mon Gat'ô Pâtisserie has closed its Port Credit shop at 150 Lakeshore Rd. W. and reopened at a new address in Streetsville. The outlet reported the bakery, known for coffee, pastries, gourmet cookies and cakes, announced the move on Instagram last week. Mon Gat'ô thanked its Port Credit customers in the post, saying the community had welcomed and supported the business, insauga.com said. The bakery's new home is at 237 Queen St. S., a space previously occupied by Streetsville Travel and briefly by a juice and coffee shop, according to the report. Its former Port Credit location, insauga.com noted, had been home to a La Diperie ice cream and desserts shop before Mon Gat'ô moved in.

items.title: Coroner's inquest to examine police-involved shooting death of Mississauga man
items.summary: A coroner's inquest, initially set for Thursday, will begin on Friday to examine the circumstances surrounding the death of a man who was shot in the head by police west of Toronto nearly seven years ago.

items.title: OLG Confirms $38-Million Gold Ball Jackpot Ticket Sold in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, a Lotto 6/49 ticket sold in Mississauga has won the $38-million Gold Ball jackpot from Wednesday night's draw. The outlet reported the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation said the winning ticket was purchased in Mississauga, making it one of the province's largest lottery wins this year. The Nov. 11 draw also produced other sizable prizes across Ontario, CityNews said, including a $1-million Encore prize won by a ticket sold in the Leeds and Grenville region. The identity of the $38-million winner has not yet been released, according to the report. CityNews noted that lottery winners must have their tickets validated through OLG before any prize can be officially awarded.

items.title: Police Close Cawthra Road Lanes After Driver Hits Traffic Pole in Life-Threatening Crash
items.summary: According to insauga.com, a driver was rushed to hospital after a single-vehicle crash into a traffic pole at Bloor Street and Cawthra Road in Mississauga early Thursday. The outlet reported Peel Regional Police said the male driver was transported to a local trauma centre in life-threatening condition; officers released no further details about him. Southbound traffic on Cawthra Road at Bloor Street was redirected eastbound, while westbound traffic from Cawthra Road was shut down, insauga.com said. Police asked drivers to use alternate routes while crews worked at the scene, according to the report. The collision was reported to police at about 3:35 a.m. on Nov. 12, insauga.com noted.

items.title: City Warns Milder El Niño Winter Could Delay Mississauga's Outdoor Ice Rinks
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a strong El Niño pattern could bring a longer, milder fall and a greater chance of extreme weather to the city this year. The city said El Niño is driven by warmer than normal ocean temperatures and that climate change may be intensifying its effects. Mississauga could see a slower start to winter with more freeze-thaw days, which the city said may delay or alter some services. The city operates four artificial outdoor rinks, and warmer temperatures make it harder to form and maintain ice on them, according to the city. Mississauga said it may delay or pause rink openings for safety reasons and urged residents to call 905-615-3200 ext. RINK or check signage at natural, volunteer-run rinks before heading out. The city also warned that repeated freezing and thawing can weaken trees and cause branches to fall.
